search_scope: soft masks and distributed sparse plasticity
known_limits: This is a targeted decision review rather than a systematic or exhaustive review.
No reviewed paper tests Zero's exact 4.85M-parameter character transformer, quantity-routing task, replay authority, and language gates.
Results from classifiers, large pretrained transformers, and other continual-learning regimes transfer to Zero only as mechanisms to test, not as outcome guarantees.

works.citation: Kirkpatrick et al. (2017), Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
works.locator: Figure 1 and Eq. 3, p. 3; Fisher approximation caveat, supplementary discussion
supports: A quadratic penalty can make parameters selectively resistant to change in proportion to estimated old-task importance while leaving less important parameters more plastic.
The source explicitly frames this as slow learning for crucial weights and faster learning for weakly constrained weights.
works.experimental_setting: Sequential supervised classification and Atari reinforcement-learning tasks.
limitations: The diagonal Fisher approximation can underestimate uncertainty and treat estimated null directions as safer than they are.
The experiments do not establish language preservation or the correct importance estimator for Zero.
works.direct_design_consequence: Use replay-derived importance only as a prospective stiffness signal; retain direct replay and frozen language gates as authority, and include a floor on plasticity so an estimated nullspace is not mistaken for proven safety.

works.citation: Zenke, Poole, and Ganguli (2017), Continual Learning Through Synaptic Intelligence
works.locator: Sections 2-3 and Eqs. 3-5; discussion of noisy contribution estimates
supports: Per-synapse importance can be estimated online from each parameter's contribution along the optimization path and used in a quadratic consolidation penalty.
The method is an explicit soft alternative to hard freezing or a single reduced learning rate.
works.experimental_setting: Sequential classification, including permuted MNIST, with feed-forward and deep networks.
limitations: Noisy stochastic gradients can overestimate importance; damping and regularization strength are material hyperparameters.
The source does not validate the estimator on generative language behavior or under Zero's replay projection.
works.direct_design_consequence: Do not use raw path-integral importance without damping and stability checks; compare it with replay-gradient Fisher before choosing a Zero plasticity profile.

works.citation: Howard and Ruder (2018), Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
supports: Discriminative fine-tuning uses smaller learning rates in lower layers, and gradual unfreezing opens layers in stages rather than imposing a permanent hard cutoff.
Last-layer-only fine-tuning severely underfit in the reported classifier experiments.
works.experimental_setting: Pretrained AWD-LSTM language models fine-tuned for text classification.
limitations: The architecture is recurrent and the target is classification rather than character-level generation or continual faculty acquisition.
Gradual unfreezing eventually trains all layers; it does not prove a fixed importance-weighted profile.
works.direct_design_consequence: Treat a top-only boundary as a baseline and compare it against a distributed layerwise schedule; do not infer that lower layers should remain permanently frozen.

works.citation: Houlsby et al. (2019), Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
works.locator: Figure 2 and Section 2.1; Figure 6 ablations, pp. 6-7
supports: Near-identity bottleneck adapters distributed after attention and feed-forward sublayers can approach full fine-tuning performance while the base transformer remains frozen.
Single-layer adapter ablations had small effects while removing all adapters caused large drops, showing a cumulative distributed adaptation effect.
works.experimental_setting: BERT transfer to GLUE classification tasks and SQuAD, with task-specific adapters.
limitations: Adapters add parameters and task-specific paths; Zero currently expects one shared generative model and checkpoint format.
Base-weight preservation does not by itself prove preservation when the adapter is active.
works.direct_design_consequence: Keep distributed adapters as a higher-cost fallback; any test must measure active-model replay/language behavior and account for architecture and checkpoint changes.

works.citation: Chaudhry et al. (2019), Efficient Lifelong Learning with A-GEM
supports: A replay-memory gradient can define a local constraint, with a proposed update projected only when it conflicts with retained-task performance.
An averaged constraint reduces the cost of per-task gradient constraints.
works.experimental_setting: Continual supervised classification with episodic replay memory.
limitations: The guarantee is local to the sampled memory gradient, not an external language distribution.
Averaging can hide damage to individual replay slices.
works.direct_design_consequence: Keep projection as a local guard diagnostic, but retain Zero's per-slice functional gate and test whether plasticity scaling changes the projected direction's useful signal.

works.citation: Farajtabar et al. (2020), Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
supports: Projecting new-task gradients orthogonally to stored old-output gradient directions can locally minimize interference with old predictions.
A subset of stored gradient directions can be used as an approximation.
works.experimental_setting: Sequential classification benchmarks with stored output-gradient bases.
limitations: Stored old gradients are only local proxies as parameters move, and storage grows with tasks or basis size.
The source does not show that projection creates missing new-task gradient signal or fixes a poorly chosen trainable subspace.
works.direct_design_consequence: Instrument pre/post-projection new-task alignment and retained-output change separately; do not interpret a small removal fraction as proof that the remaining subspace has adequate learning capacity.

works.citation: Warstadt et al. (2020), BLiMP: The Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for English
supports: Controlled minimal pairs provide a targeted screen for selected grammatical preferences.
works.experimental_setting: English grammatical acceptability across 67 paradigms and 12 phenomenon categories.
limitations: BLiMP does not measure general coherence, semantics, reasoning, or the quantity-routing faculty.
Aggregate accuracy can hide phenomenon-specific regressions.
works.direct_design_consequence: Never use BLiMP to construct or tune a plasticity profile; use it once, prospectively and conjunctively, only after a quantity/replay candidate is frozen.

works.citation: Xu et al. (2021), Raise a Child in Large Language Model: Towards Effective and Generalizable Fine-tuning
works.locator: Figure 1 and Sections 2.2-2.3; lowest-Fisher ablation in Section 4.4
supports: A fixed gradient mask can update a distributed parameter subset while the forward pass still uses the full network.
For new-task generalization, selecting high new-task Fisher parameters outperformed selecting the lowest-Fisher parameters in the reported ablation.
works.experimental_setting: Large pretrained transformer fine-tuning on GLUE and NLI tasks.
limitations: The task-driven Fisher measures importance to the new task, not safety for an old language behavior.
Random masks sometimes improved over vanilla fine-tuning, so benefits can include regularization rather than causal localization.
works.direct_design_consequence: Combine old-task risk with new-task relevance; selecting only low replay importance could allocate flexible capacity that carries no quantity signal.

works.citation: Guo, Rush, and Kim (2021), Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning with Diff Pruning
works.locator: Table 1; Sections 6.1-6.3 and Figure 2, p. 6; footnote 15
supports: Sparse task-specific difference vectors distributed across a frozen pretrained model matched full fine-tuning on the reported NLP benchmarks at about 0.5% changed base parameters.
Different tasks selected different cross-layer distributions of changes.
works.experimental_setting: BERT transfer across GLUE and SQuAD using learned sparse difference vectors.
limitations: The method adds training memory for difference and mask variables and was evaluated on discriminative tasks, not continual generative preservation.
Sparsity does not itself establish which old behavior remains intact.
works.direct_design_consequence: Prefer a prospectively fixed, cross-layer mask over a top-FFN-only mask; the paper reports much worse performance when diff pruning is restricted to fully connected layers after self-attention.

works.citation: Meng et al. (2022), Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
supports: Causal tracing and localized MLP edits can identify and change some factual associations while optimizing locality.
works.experimental_setting: Factual recall and model editing in large pretrained GPT models.
limitations: The strongest localization is in middle-layer MLPs for factual recall, not Zero's top FFN for operation routing.
Localized factual edits do not establish global language preservation or a universal safe layer boundary.
works.direct_design_consequence: Require causal ablations or prospective masks for Zero; do not infer a quantity-routing locus from aggregate displacement or FFN interpretability alone.

works.citation: Eldan and Li (2023), TinyStories: How Small Can Language Models Be and Still Speak Coherent English?
supports: A bounded synthetic-story distribution is relevant to measuring small language models, and the paper evaluates more than loss alone.
works.experimental_setting: Small language models trained and evaluated on synthetic short English stories.
limitations: The distribution is synthetic, narrow, and intentionally simple.
Bits per byte cannot alone establish coherent generation or general English preservation.
works.direct_design_consequence: Keep TinyStories loss as a frozen, bounded regression screen; do not expose it to profile selection and do not broaden claims beyond that distribution.

works.citation: Liu and Niehues (2025), Conditions for Catastrophic Forgetting in Multilingual Translation
supports: Forgetting depends on model scale and fine-tuning data volume, so it must be measured under the actual training regime.
LoRA and full fine-tuning showed comparable forgetting under the controlled translation conditions.
works.experimental_setting: Multilingual translation adaptation across model sizes and data volumes.
limitations: The models, languages, task, and scale differ from Zero.
The result is counterevidence to parameter-count safety, not a claim that LoRA never helps preservation.
works.direct_design_consequence: Treat every parameter-efficient method as an adaptation mechanism, not a preservation guarantee; the unchanged replay and language gates remain decisive.

established_evidence: Soft, importance-weighted consolidation, layerwise learning schedules, gradient projection, sparse masks, and distributed adapters are established method families in their reported settings.
Top- or last-layer-only adaptation can underfit, and distributed adaptation can matter cumulatively across layers.
Reduced trainable parameter count is not, by itself, evidence of reduced forgetting.
BLiMP and TinyStories loss are bounded screens, not comprehensive language-preservation proofs.
analogy_to_zero: Per-weight stiffness is a direct conceptual match to graded stickiness, but the importance estimator and optimization geometry must be validated in Zero.
Distributed sparse diffs and adapters suggest that useful flexibility may need to exist throughout the network, but their discriminative large-model results do not predict Zero's effect size.
Projection methods explain how to reduce local interference; they do not supply absent quantity-routing signal.
project_specific_hypotheses: Zero's best next trainable subspace may be a cross-layer profile based jointly on new-task relevance and old-replay risk.
Embeddings should begin highly sticky because Q2.6 assigns them the largest replay-drift and Fisher-weighted-drift signals, but that attribution is correlational rather than causal.
Q2.7 failed because top-FFN isolation removed necessary cross-layer coordination or routing capacity, not because those top FFN weights moved too little.
synthesis.targeted_review_trigger: Perform an additional targeted review only if the proposed intervention changes family materially, such as dynamic masks, optimizer-state consolidation, or a new adapter architecture.
